# The programs and chain accounts the client's LiteSVM tests load (js/test/world.mjs), pinned by hash: the outside
# programs as the Solana clusters run them, the loot program as devnet runs it (the build release.json pins), the
# oracle's queue as it is on mainnet, and a small transfer hook made for the tests.
#
# The tests refuse a file whose sha256 differs from its line here. `npm run fixtures` (scripts/fetch-fixtures.mjs)
# downloads every program that is missing or differs, read-only, and checks it; `--check` checks what is here without
# the network. Programs read from a cluster are not committed (upstream binaries, and loot.so is the program's own
# build): .gitignore keeps them out. The accounts (mainnet/queue.json) and test_hook.so are committed.
#
# Mainnet is where loot will deploy, so the outside programs are mainnet's builds. loot.so is devnet's, the only
# cluster it runs on; its sha256 and bytes are release.json's sbfSha256 and sbfBytes, and `--check` says so when they
# part. test_hook.so (cluster `-`, loader `local`) is never deployed: a 27-line pinocchio program built alongside the
# loot program's source, committed here as a binary. Token-2022 calls it on every transfer of a mint that names it; it
# counts transfers in an account it owns, refuses a transfer of 13, and marks the count if any account arrives signed.
#
# Columns: file (under js/test/fixtures), address, cluster it was read from, loader (`upgradeable`, `v2` for
# BPFLoader2, `account` for an account's JSON, `local` for a file made for the tests), sha256 of the file, its bytes,
# the slot (a program's last deployment; an account's read), and the release its security.txt names (`-` when none).
#
# file                           address                                      cluster loader      sha256 bytes slot release
